claims.text: The initial material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr suffers from inadequate oxygen resistance.
A thin aluminide-based surface coating can be deposited by pack cementation or sputtering.
Applying a thin aluminide-based coating to cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance.
The aluminide coating will promote formation of a continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale during high-temperature exposure.
The aluminide coating preferentially oxidizes to form a slow-growing alumina layer.
The alumina layer acts as a diffusion barrier against oxygen ingress.
Suppressing oxygen ingress will mitigate deleterious internal oxidation.
The coating can provide oxidation protection without altering the alloy's bulk properties.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, coated specimens will have significantly lower oxide-scale thickness than untreated specimens.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, coated specimens will have significantly lower oxidation weight gain than untreated specimens.
The coated alloy will preserve its room-temperature mechanical performance after 5 hours in air at 800 °C.
The coated alloy will preserve its high-temperature mechanical performance after 5 hours in air at 800 °C.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undergoes substantial oxidation leading to pesting under conditions similar to 800 °C in air for 5 hours.
The applicable loading boundary is a strain-rate range of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1, corresponding to previous tensile tests.
The proposed applicability boundary is atmospheric air near 800 °C for up to 5 hours.

contradictions.description: The conditions and boundary imply applicability under mechanical loading at specified strain rates, but the experiment describes an unloaded oxidation exposure followed by tensile testing, so it does not test simultaneous oxidation-and-loading behavior.
